text:
courtney: spun up sg1-mix rack this morning (4 hosts: 2x A30, 2x A4000, 1x T4 sidecar). planning perf validation & handoff.
devin: ok. targets? latency/throughput/cost we should be aiming for on the quantized 6B baseline?
courtney: baseline: p95 <= 40ms for 256-token inference, sustained throughput 200 req/s across rack (all GPUs aggregated) with 16 concurrency streams. soft cost target ~$0.0007/token.
rahul: quick hardware probe shows mixed PCIe gen (A30s on gen4 x16, A4000 on gen3 x8). also saw inconsistent MPS state across hosts. ran dmesg on a failing A4000 and got:```[  8.912345] NVRM: RmInitAdapter failed! (0x0)
[  8.912350] nvidia: probe of 0000:af:00.0 failed with error -5```
devin: that looks like driver/kernel mismatch. which driver is on those nodes?
rahul: several hosts on nvidia-driver-525.85, a couple provisioned with 530.54 by default. infra-bot suggests trying 535.xx series for better A30/A4000 parity.
infra-bot: queued tasks: perf-canary-256 (canary nodes: sg1-node-02, sg1-node-06), driver-compat-scan-535, nvlink-check. Will post aggregated results.
courtney: ran nvidia-smi -L on sg1-node-02 (A30):```GPU 0: NVIDIA A30 (UUID: GPU-aaaaaaaa-bbbb)
GPU 1: NVIDIA T4 (UUID: GPU-cccccccc-dddd)```
devin: micro-bench command used for canary:
```perf-test --model rdinfer-6b-quant --quant int8 --concurrency 16 --tokens 256 --duration 180```
infra-bot: canary summary: sg1-node-02 (A30): p50=12ms p95=28ms tput=142 req/s; sg1-node-06 (A4000): p50=20ms p95=46ms tput=78 req/s. nvlink-check: A30 ok, A4000 link retrain warnings.
rahul: A4000 throughput lagging. dug into BIOS/firmware: A4000 hosts defaulted to PCIe gen3 x8. vendor offers a 'performance' BIOS profile to force gen4 where supported but needs maintenance window. MPS also off on half the A4000s — enabling MPS raised concurrency in local tests.
courtney: proposed action items:
- standardize nvidia-driver to 535.17 across rack (rollback older 525.x)
- schedule BIOS profile change to enable PCIe gen4 where supported (contact provider)
- enable NVIDIA MPS on inference hosts for soak
- runtime batcher tweaks for heterogeneous fleet: lower max tokens on A4000-backed routes
- 6h soak run after changes, collect traces and kernel logs
devin: kernel/userland tweaks to try during soak: set irq affinity for inference cores, and lower swappiness. example commands:
```echo 1 > /proc/sys/kernel/irqbalance_enabled || true
for cpu in 0 1 2 3; do echo $cpu > /proc/irq/XX/smp_affinity_list; done
sysctl -w vm.swappiness=10```
rahul: also enable the runtime envs for batcher: `REDWOOD_BATCHER_MAX_TOKENS=512` and `REDWOOD_BATCHER_CONCURRENCY_LIMIT=16` for A30, and `REDWOOD_BATCHER_MAX_TOKENS=256` `REDWOOD_BATCHER_CONCURRENCY_LIMIT=8` for A4000 nodes.
ops-sre: I can slot a 30m maintenance tonight 2026-03-20T01:00Z to flip BIOS profile for sg1 racks. Need confirmation to drain and disable autoscaling during change.
courtney: yes please drain and disable autoscaling. mark nodes as draining and set traffic weight to 0 for the duration.
infra-bot: post-canary after driver 535 + MPS enabled:
- sg1-node-02 (A30): p95=26ms throughput=155 req/s
- sg1-node-06 (A4000): p95=39ms throughput=102 req/s
- nvlink-check: A4000 warnings reduced after driver update
devin: much better. A4000 still lower throughput but now within latency SLO. routing implications: prefer A30 for latency-sensitive routes, A4000 for batch/background. can we add a routing tag?
courtney: yes, we'll apply node labels: `sg1:hardware=latency-optimized` for A30 hosts and `sg1:hardware=batch-optimized` for A4000. also add runtime route config to prefer low-latency nodes when request header `x-rd-priority=lowlat` set.
ops-sre: preparing handoff note with artifacts:
- driver image: nvidia-driver-535.17
- kernel tested: 5.15.0-103 (no regressions observed in 48h soak)
- node labels applied: sg1:latency-opt(A30), sg1:batch-opt(A4000)
- soak logs: s3://redwood-perf/sg1/soak/2145678901/
- maintenance window: 2026-03-20T01:00Z (30m)
- alerts: create rule -> if p95 > 50ms for 10m => notify eng-sre and ops-sre
tara: adding runbook note: nvlink retrain warnings on A4000 can usually be resolved by firmware update or PCIe retrain; include diagnostic commands in runbook (lspci -vv, nvidia-smi dmon).
courtney: assigning follow-ups: @rahul verify perf traces and kernel logs, @devin implement routing label + runtime config, @ops-sre perform BIOS change and confirm post-soak. after successful 6h soak we hand off to ops-sre.
ops-sre: will validate soak artifacts tomorrow morning and post final status. closing loop once validated.
courtney: thanks all — I'll update the sg1 bring-up runbook with these steps and link artifacts. :white_check_mark:
